principles: Host-neutral workflow commands stay outside Codex/Claude-specific namespaces.
Learning artifacts remain advisory and non-authoritative; gate evidence stays separate.
Reviewed batches must be bound by deterministic digests before any mutation.
Fix real correctness gaps: duplicate source consumption, stale batch apply, candidate/runtime confusion, and unsafe auto-activation.
Keep logic consistent with existing single-playbook commands instead of adding parallel semantics.
drivers: The user needs historical experience to become usable playbook candidates without duplicate source counting.
B-01df only added source lineage audit; the rest of the execution plan is still unimplemented.
Auto-promotion is useful only after real outcomes and reviewed policy exist, so V1 must fail closed.

options.name: Status-only observation
cons: No digest-guarded path from seeds to candidates
Does not solve the user-visible repeat-mistake failure mode

options.name: Deduped seed observe with digest-guarded proposal and approval
pros: Turns lineage audit into a controlled candidate pipeline
Prevents observe/apply drift and duplicate canonical source writes
Preserves candidate inertness and explicit activation boundary
cons: Requires new helper types and smoke coverage
Does not fully automate active playbook promotion in V1

options.name: Immediate automatic activation
cons: Risks injecting unreviewed learning into runtime guidance

chosen: Deduped seed observe with digest-guarded proposal and approval
rationale: This is the smallest path that closes the real correctness gap: historical learning can become reviewed candidates without duplicate source counting or unsafe auto-activation.

preMortem.scenario: Batch apply writes a different seed set than the one reviewed.
preMortem.trigger: Learning sources change between observe and apply.
preMortem.consequence: Operators approve candidates they did not review.
preMortem.mitigation: Require observeDigest on apply and fail closed on drift.

preMortem.scenario: Candidate playbooks leak into runtime guidance.
preMortem.trigger: Runtime memory helper treats candidates like active playbooks.
preMortem.consequence: Unreviewed candidate advice influences agents as if active.
preMortem.mitigation: Add runtime consumption verification that asserts candidates remain pending learning only.

preMortem.scenario: DONE success is counted as helped for an unexposed candidate.
preMortem.trigger: Settlement hook conflates story success with candidate usefulness.
preMortem.consequence: Promotion recommendations are inflated by unrelated DONE outcomes.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep DONE settlement disabled by default and test that helped requires explicit exposure/verdict source.

preMortem.scenario: Auto-promotion becomes an accidental activation path.
preMortem.trigger: A future flag or command omits reviewed policy/outcome/lineage checks.
preMortem.consequence: Candidates become active without enough evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Implement V2 command as fail-closed guard and document disabled posture in status.
